copy.anchor: Build starts from a problem you have tested. From the blueprint altitude, the team draws what a first release must do, cuts the scope to that, and builds it in reviewed cycles. (/program/build/, /program/who-its-for/)
copy.convey: Blueprint altitude: a plan drawn before it is built. It reads as drawn, not constructed.
copy.avoid: Circuit traces, screens, a finished building, anything that looks like a result.

prompts.object: Editorial still life photograph of a hand-built tabletop model made of paper, card, matte ceramic and brushed steel, photographed as a physical object on a plain pale surface, soft north-window light with long gentle shadows, 50mm lens, shallow depth of field, matte film grade with lifted whites. Straight-down view of a large blueprint: pale linework of a six-sided hexagonal grid frame on deep blue card with fine dimension lines. Subject centred with a generous quiet margin around it, every key element near the middle of the frame. Color palette: crisp white and pale mist-blue surfaces, deep blue and slate, soft grey. There is exactly one amber object in the frame: one small six-sided hexagon tile in amber glass resting at a crossing of two lines near the middle of the blueprint. All other objects are white, grey, blue or slate. No text, no logos, no writing.
prompts.figure: Editorial documentary photograph of a calm working session around a hand-built tabletop model made of paper, card, matte ceramic and brushed steel, soft north-window daylight, 50mm lens, shallow depth of field, matte film grade with lifted whites. Framed from the chest down so that no head is in the frame: one person only, in a navy sweater, seated at a pale drafting table, forearms on the table, tracing the hexagonal grid frame with a blue pencil, in front of a deep blue blueprint card with pale hexagonal linework. Subject centred with a generous quiet margin around it, every key element near the middle of the frame. Color palette: crisp white and pale mist-blue surfaces, deep blue and slate, soft grey. There is exactly one amber object in the frame: one small six-sided hexagon tile of the model in amber glass at a crossing of two lines. All other objects are white, grey, blue or slate. No text, no logos, no writing.
